source.title: When Does Bigger Help? A Controlled Study of LLM Scale for Ontology Learning
source.authors: Hamed Babaei Giglou; S. Auer; Jennifer D'Souza

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream ontology-learning performance across model sizes using a controlled benchmark, a different measure and setting from pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original scaling-law studies and other scaling work, but those cited results are not this study’s results. The study reports separate precision, recall, and F1 scores; rows below record F1, the main outcome for downstream performance. It holds retrieval and prompting conditions constant, but does not report pretraining losses, compute budgets, power-law fits, or extrapolation tests.
record.test_reason: The study measures downstream ontology-learning F1 across a within-family Qwen3.5 size sweep (0.8B–27B dense, plus 35B-A3B and 122B-A10B MoE) under fixed retrieval and prompting. This is a new downstream setting that bears on V6 (downstream performance improving with scale). It reports no pretraining loss, compute, fits or extrapolation, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. T3 fits better than T2: it is a new task setting, not a different method aimed at the originals' loss question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add four points: the authors find scale mainly improves precision rather than recall, with the main inflection between 9B and 27B; taxonomy discovery benefits from larger (MoE) capacity; architecture and alignment or lineage can outweigh nominal parameter count; and model size alone is an insufficient selection criterion for ontology learning.
record.recipe_differences: This is a downstream zero-shot RAG benchmark of ontology-learning F1 across model sizes and lineages, not a pretraining-loss scaling-law experiment or compute-optimal training sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies across task and ontology; the paper also reports differing results for dense versus MoE models and across model releases. It holds the embedding model, retrieval configuration, prompts, decoding conditions, datasets, and metrics constant.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched nominal size, Qwen3.6-27B differs sharply from Qwen3.5-27B (MatWerk TT 36.62 vs 58.14; MFOEM TT 50.00 vs 46.51).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model release or lineage can change downstream task scores independently of parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: Among GPT releases (sizes unstated), the older GPT-5.5 outperforms the GPT-5.6 variants on most tasks. GPT-5.6-Luna is over-conservative (MFOEM TT recall 5.26%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment or release changes alter downstream behaviour without a parameter-scale change.

record.peer_reviewed: WOP at ISWC’26: 17th Workshop on Ontology Design and Patterns at the International Semantic Web Conference, as stated in the paper.
record.problems: The evidence concerns only four ontology datasets and three zero-shot RAG tasks. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Results depend on the chosen retrieval and prompting setup; OBI experiments retain only 20% of the ontological data. Parameter scaling is not isolated from architecture for the MoE comparisons, and proprietary GPT parameter counts are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: The tables report additional models and task–ontology combinations, plus precision and recall alongside F1. To stay within the row limit, rows retain the dense Qwen3.5 scale sweep for selected task–ontology settings and the principal reported MoE and matched-release comparisons; other table entries and secondary metrics are omitted. See Tables 4–5. GPT release comparisons are not cataloged as scale rows because their parameter sizes are not stated.

untested.parts: No relation between task performance and pretraining loss. No fitted scaling curve, and no test of whether small-model results predict large-model results. Tested only on zero-shot RAG ontology learning over released instruction-tuned checkpoints whose training data and compute are not controlled.
No loss at fixed parameter count with varied shape. The dense vs MoE comparison is not a shape test.
No other modality or training regime.
No exponents or fitting choices studied.

missing.what: OBI taxonomy discovery F1 across the Qwen3.5 sweep: 6.19 (0.8B–4B) → 6.61 (9B) → 11.59 (27B) → 22.07 (122B-A10B).
Non-taxonomic RE on MFOEM (7.43→11.24 at 27B, 8.00 at 122B) and MatWerk (6.90→12.24 at 27B, 7.44 at 122B). Dense models rise, MoE models fall back.
Precision rises with scale while recall stays flat or falls (e.g. MatWerk TT precision 14.29→43.86, recall 100→86.21).
2B and 4B rows for settings other than MatWerk term typing. They are identical or near-identical to 0.8B, which documents the plateau.

record.verdict_notes: Downstream only. The models are released instruction-tuned checkpoints with uncontrolled training data and compute, so the size sweep is not a controlled scaling experiment. Term-typing sets are tiny (tens of terms), no uncertainty is reported, and OBI uses a 20% subset, so small F1 differences may be noise. No curves are fitted, so the 'predictably' part of V6 cannot be judged beyond monotonicity. MoE total vs active parameters makes 'scale' ambiguous for r06, r10, r14 and r27–r29.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No loss predictions from small runs or comparison with much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
The study compares some architectures, but does not measure pretraining loss at fixed parameter count or systematically vary depth and width.
No other modality or training regime is tested.
Tests zero-shot RAG ontology-learning tasks only. It does not relate task performance to pretraining loss or test predictability on other downstream task families.
No scaling-law exponents, fitting choices, compute-optimal splits, or fitted pretraining-loss curves are studied.

relationships.condition: Qwen3.5 dense 0.8B→27B on MatWerk/OBI term typing and MFOEM/MatWerk taxonomy discovery; 122B-A10B and 35B-A3B MoE on taxonomy discovery
relationships.reason: F1 rises with size: MatWerk TT 25.00→58.14, OBI TT 16.47→31.07, MFOEM TD 8.98→24.41, MatWerk TD 7.94→23.05 (r04, r05, r12, r13, r17, r18, r21, r22, r28).
relationships.display_finding: F1 rises from 25.00 to 58.14 for MatWerk term typing, 16.47 to 31.07 for OBI term typing, 8.98 to 24.41 for MFOEM taxonomy discovery, and 7.94 to 23.05 for MatWerk taxonomy discovery.

relationships.reason: Gains are threshold-like, not smooth: F1 is flat or near-flat up to 4B–9B, and most of the gain appears at 9B→27B (r02, r03, r08, r16, r20).
relationships.display_finding: F1 stayed flat or nearly flat through 4B–9B, with most improvement appearing from 9B to 27B.

relationships.condition: Term typing with larger-total-parameter MoE models, and MFOEM term typing generally
relationships.reason: 122B-A10B and 35B-A3B score below 27B dense on term typing (r06, r14, r27). MFOEM TT barely moves with scale (r09, r10).
relationships.display_finding: The 122B-A10B and 35B-A3B models scored below 27B dense on term typing, while MFOEM term typing barely changed with scale.

relationships.condition: MDS non-taxonomic relation extraction across the Qwen3.5 sweep
relationships.reason: F1 is flat from 0.8B to 122B (1.22 vs 1.27); the authors call this 'almost no improvement' (r24, r25, r26, r29).
relationships.display_finding: F1 remained nearly flat from 0.8B to 122B, changing from 1.22 to 1.27.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3.5 dense models on MFOEM and MatWerk taxonomy discovery, and term typing through 27B in MatWerk and OBI
reader_labels.reason: F1 rises across the reported sizes in these settings, with a pronounced MatWerk term-typing gain at 27B (r01, r03-r05, r11-r13, r15-r17, r19-r21).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3.5 term typing across MFOEM and OBI, and MatWerk term typing at the largest MoE scale
reader_labels.reason: Gains are modest or non-monotonic in some settings; the 122B MoE term-typing scores fall below the 27B dense scores, and OBI also declines from 27B to 122B (r06, r08-r10, r14).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: MDS non-taxonomic relationship extraction in the Qwen3.5 scale sweep
reader_labels.reason: The reported F1 values remain essentially flat from 0.8B to 122B, and the 9B and 27B results are below the 0.8B reference (r23-r26).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on selected term-typing and relationship-extraction settings
reader_labels.reason: The MoE model is below the dense 27B term-typing result on MatWerk and shows no meaningful MDS relationship-extraction gain, though it improves on MFOEM taxonomy discovery (r27-r29).
